Cancer/Oncology Species: Dog Current status: Open and enrolling Study title Evaluation of xenogeneic CAR-T cell therapy for canine CD20+ B cell lymphoma Purpose of study The current standard of care for canine B-cell lymphoma is a multi-agent (CHOP) chemotherapy protocol, which require weekly trips to the vet over approximately 5 months, costs $7k-12k, and puts 80-90% of dogs into remission for 9-12 months before relapse. Canine B-cell lymphoma resembles human non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma, a cancer now successfully treated with Chimeric Antigen Receptor T cells (CAR-T cells). In this study, LEAH Labs is sponsoring an pilot trial to test the safety of a CAR-T cell therapy product in dogs with B-cell lymphoma; with the hopes to find a more cost-effective and efficacious therapy for dogs with this disease. Eligibility criteria Eligible dogs must match these criteria: body weight of at least 10kgs (22lbs) any breed, except boxers Clinical presentation: Peripheral multicentric lymphoma (minimum of 4 target peripheral lymph nodes evaluable) Have naïve or relapsed disease, substage A only fine needle aspirate (in-house or reference lab) consistent with lymphoblastic/high grade lymphoma performance status 0-1   Concurrent medications of note: Immunomodulatory drugs (Apoquel, mycophenolate, cyclosporine, azathioprine) are not allowed Cytopoint  is allowable and can be maintained for the study period Prednisone use: not allowed if it's used for substage B disease patient must be able to taper off 72 hours prior to CAR-T administration and remain off for duration of study Procedures Scre
